pl-l4d1c10-d1e115.summary: Asks whether infants who died before the eighth day, before which circumcision was not performed under the Law, were saved, and answers as is held about infants who die before baptism, who are lost.
claims: Infants dying before circumcision were lost, as unbaptized infants are.

pl-l4d1c10-d1e118.summary: Quotes Bede: the one who now cries through the Gospel 'unless one is reborn of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God' cried long ago through the Law, 'the soul whose foreskin is not circumcised shall perish'. Perhaps, under the pressure of death, they circumcised children before the eighth day without sin, as is now done with baptism in the Church.
claims: Both circumcision and baptism were necessary for salvation.
Emergency circumcision before the eighth day may have been lawful.

pl-l4d1c10.summary: Asks whether infants who died before the eighth day, before circumcision under the Law, were saved, and answers as with infants who die before baptism, who are lost. Bede: the one who now says 'unless one is reborn of water and the Spirit' said in the Law that the uncircumcised soul will perish; perhaps, under threat of death, children were circumcised before the eighth day without sin, as is now done with baptism.
claims: Infants dying uncircumcised before the eighth day were lost, as unbaptized infants are.
Circumcision before the eighth day in danger of death was perhaps permitted.
